name: Bláthnat

attributes.attribute: Irish goddess whose name means little flower
daughter of Midir, king of the Irish fairies
brought from the Otherworld by the hero Cúchulainn
stole her cattle and cauldron and buried her
chose the life of a convent

sources: Condren, Mary. The Serpent and the Goddess: Women, Religion and Power in Ancient Ireland. San Francisco: Harper & Row, 1989, 71.
MacCulloch, J. A. The Religion of the Ancient Celts. London: Constable, 1911.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Bláthnat is an Irish goddess. Her name means little flower. A tale names her the daughter of Midir. Midir was the king of the Irish fairies. Another tale says she was the child of Ulster's ruler. That ruler was Concobar Mac Nessa. The hero Cúchulainn carried Bláthnat from the Otherworld. He carried her magic cattle and a cauldron too. His comrade in that raid was Cú Roí. Cú Roí then stole the cattle and the cauldron. Cú Roí also buried the maiden. She did not live well beside Cú Roí. She planned his murder within a year. Bláthnat took the hero Cúchulainn as her lover. She told him the secret to kill her husband. This makes her the Irish form of the Welsh Blodeuwedd. Cú Roí's poet Fercheertne pushed her over a cliff. He died in the same act. She later chose the forgiven life of a nun.

okr.objective: Describe Bláthnat, the Irish goddess who turned against the lord who kept her.
key_results: Cúchulainn carried her from the Otherworld.
Cú Roí stole her treasure and buried her.
Bláthnat told her lover how to kill Cú Roí.
